sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know ordering markers such as *primero* and *además* from A2 Unit 28, and *por un lado* from B1 Unit 23. They put events and ideas in order. The return to elected government is a long list of countries and years, so they help the reader follow it.

items.spanish: Primero volvieron Ecuador y Perú; después volvieron Bolivia y Argentina.
items.english: First Ecuador and Peru returned; then Bolivia and Argentina returned.

items.spanish: Finalmente, en 1990, Chile tuvo un presidente civil.
items.english: Finally, in 1990, Chile had a civilian president.

items.spanish: Por un lado, hubo elecciones; por otro lado, los militares conservaron poder.
items.english: On one hand there were elections; on the other, the military kept power.

items.spanish: Además, los nuevos gobiernos recibieron una gran deuda.
items.english: Besides, the new governments received a large debt.

sections.content: Use *primero*, *después* and *finalmente* for a sequence, and a comma after the marker. *Por un lado* needs *por otro lado* (or *por otra parte*) to complete the pair. *Además* adds one more point to the same idea.
